title: `textureSize` being reported as `(1, 1)` with Forward+ renderer
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in `v4.4.stable.mono.official [4c311cbee]`, `v4.5.dev2.mono.official [af2c71397]` ### System information Godot v4.4.stable.mono - macOS Sequoia (15.4.1) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M2 Ultra (Apple8) - Apple M2 Ultra (24 threads) ### Issue description Yesterday, my game looked/worked fine, then I ran an incremental macOS upgrade (i.e. I was already on Sequoia and probably got a new minor version), and now it seems like `textureSize` is being reported incorrectly in my shaders in Godot. The repro is very simple; attach the shader below, and with the Forward+ renderer, you'll see that `textureSize` reports a `(1, 1)` texture. With the Compatibility renderer, it correctly reports `(128, 128)`: I suspect this is _actually_ a driver issue, but I'm not well-versed in this realm and wanted to file this here just in case it's something that the Godot engine should address. Plus, other people may search for something like this. ### Steps to reproduce - Make a scene with a single `Sprite2D` - Set its texture to the Godot icon (which is 128x128 by default) - Add a `ShaderMaterial` to it with this shader: ```glsl shader_type canvas_item; void vertex() { } void fragment() { vec2 tex_size = vec2(textureSize(TEXTURE, 0)); if (tex_size.x == 1.0) { COLOR = vec4(1.0,0.0,1.0,1.0); } } ``` - Toggle between the Forward+ and Compatibility renderers to see two different results ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [ShaderRepro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19896251/ShaderRepro.zip)
